case_title: MRS. SARAH MATHEW v. THE INSTITUTE OF CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASES BY ITS DIRECTOR - DR. K.M. CHERIAN & ORS.
neutral_facts: The case involves a dispute regarding the period of limitation under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973. The complainant filed a complaint against the accused, and the issue arose whether the period of limitation had expired. The court examined the relevant provisions of the Code, including sections 468, 469, and 473, to determine the relevant date for computing the period of limitation. The court held that the relevant date is the date of filing of the complaint or the date of institution of prosecution, not the date on which the Magistrate takes cognizance. The court emphasized the importance of a purposive construction of the statute to ensure that the legislative intent is fulfilled and that the rights of both the complainant and the accused are balanced.
